note: Order rules behind TaskProfile.slots[].orderRuleRef. The rule is deliberately about the BINDING, not about module names: the profile must never hardcode 'A before B'. experiments/stitch-cpu-v1/recipe-builder.ts hardcodes module-aspp-v1 before module-se-v1; this profile does not, because PHASE2-SPEC section 5 says a new profile builds from module ids + bindings.

order:phase2.features.pre_pool.v1.rule: The binding's orderedModuleIds array IS the execution order. The compiled recipe applies the modules in exactly that array order, with no sorting, no name-based reordering and no implicit insertion position.

constraints.rule: one module id may appear at most once in orderedModuleIds
every module id must resolve to a pinned module source supplied by the host; a request cannot introduce a module by path
the profile must not reorder modules by their display name or by a hardcoded A/B pair
constraints.enforcedBy: compileRecipe (the implementation of this rule is that no name comparison exists in the code path)

constraints.rule: a variant name selects a PREFIX of the ordered list: 'baseline' selects none, 'a' the first, 'ab' the first two, 'abc' the first three. A variant whose length disagrees with the recipe's module count is refused.
every module in the chain preserves [B, 8, H, W] float32, so the order affects the values but never the downstream tensor contract
an unknown slot id is refused; it is never coerced onto features.pre_pool

notClaimed: Ordering is not claimed to be optimal or commutative. ASPP (multi-scale context) and SE (channel recalibration) do not commute in general; the profile records the declared order as a fact of the binding and lets the combination check decide whether the observed order matches it.
